name: Prepositions
description: Prepositions of time, place and movement, dependent prepositions after verbs, nouns and adjectives, and common prepositional phrases.

questions.title: The meeting is ___ Monday morning.
We usually go skiing ___ January.
The lesson starts ___ half past eight.
There is a bakery ___ the corner of our street.
She put the letter ___ the drawer and locked it.
The cat jumped ___ the fence and ran away.
We travelled ___ Kyiv ___ Lviv by train.
I have been waiting ___ twenty minutes.
He has lived here ___ 2015.
The keys are ___ the table, next to the lamp.
She is very good ___ mathematics.
I am afraid ___ heights.
Which preposition follows the verb 'depend'?
We arrived ___ the airport two hours early.
Match each time expression with the preposition it takes.
Match each verb with the preposition that normally follows it.
Match each adjective with the preposition it takes.
Match each preposition of movement with the sentence it fits.
pairs: He ran out of the building.
The train went through a tunnel.

questions.title: The decision was taken ___ the recommendation of the committee.
He is completely unaware ___ the difficulties ahead.
I congratulated her ___ passing the entrance exam.
They accused the supplier ___ breaking the contract.
The company invested heavily ___ renewable energy.
There is no substitute ___ regular practice.
Which sentence about prepositions contains a mistake?
options: She is married with a lawyer.
She is married to a lawyer.
She has been married for ten years.

questions.title: I am not familiar ___ that procedure.
The film differs greatly ___ the novel it is based on.
He apologised ___ me ___ arriving so late.
The results are broadly ___ line with our expectations.
We discussed the proposal ___ length before voting.
She insisted ___ paying for the meal herself.
Match each verb with the dependent preposition it requires.
Match each noun with the preposition that normally follows it.
Match each fixed phrase with its meaning.
Match each pair of phrases with the difference in meaning.
pairs: hold the same view on it

questions.title: Match each faulty phrase with the correction it needs.
The proposal was rejected ___ the grounds that it was too expensive.
Little progress has been made ___ respect to the funding gap.
The scheme was introduced ___ a view to reducing waste.
The findings are broadly consistent ___ earlier research.
Which formal phrase correctly signals an exception?
options: with the exception of the final chapter
with exception of the final chapter
in exception of the final chapter
by the exception of the final chapter

questions.title: The authorities acted ___ accordance with the new regulations.
Match each formal prepositional phrase with its plain equivalent.
pairs: in the event of a delay

questions.title: Match each academic phrase with the function it performs.
